reason: Verified per-site (RFC 0106): Ruby core `Hash#fetch` (postgresql/database_statements.rb:69) on the plain object `transactionIsolationLevels()` returns; the port now reproduces `fetch`'s semantics exactly — an absent level raises `KeyError: key not found: :bogus` — but the JS spelling (`levels[isolation]` + the KeyError throw) emits no callee named `fetch`, so no TS call can credit the Ruby one.
The whole configure body lives in `_maybeConfigureConnection`, which reads the already-parsed frozen `_sessionVariables` instead of re-fetching `@config[:variables]` per call.

configure runs while the acquire machinery still holds the connection, so the SET statements go straight to the pg.Client — routing them through internalExecute would re-enter connectBang/verify and deadlock.
The SET SESSION values are rendered by `quoteLiteral` on the raw client in `_maybeConfigureConnection`; `quote` would route back through the type-cast stack the connection is still mid-configure for.

Rails' dbconsole execs `psql` through find_cmd_and_exec; process spawning is forbidden in this package (no node:* imports, no process.*), so trails' dbconsole only builds the PG* environment the console command needs.

The body lives in postgresql/referential-integrity.ts — Rails houses it in the ReferentialIntegrity module too (postgresql/referential_integrity.rb:5-36) — and makes both calls there; the adapter member is the include seam.
Rails' with_raw_connection is re-entrant on @raw_connection; ours is not, and this runs inside the very acquire configureConnection is warming, so it takes the published `_rawConnection` directly.
The body lives in postgresql/quoting.ts, where Rails houses it too (postgresql/quoting.rb:189) and where the type_map lookup is made; the adapter member is the include seam.
Rails runs the query inside the sync reader via `||=`; trails queries are Promises, so the `queryValue` call lives in the async `warmMaxIdentifierLength` and this reader returns the warmed memo.

Rails rescues around `conn.prepare`; node-pg has no parse-only call (it Parses under the name on first Execute), so there is no prepare site here and the Parse error is translated by `_performQuery` instead.
The escape_bytea call is made in postgresql/quoting.ts:149-153, the file matching Rails' PostgreSQL::Quoting module (postgresql/quoting.rb:152); the adapter member is the include seam.
The BC `format("%04d", ...)` branch is in postgresql/quoting.ts:441, the file matching Rails' PostgreSQL::Quoting module (postgresql/quoting.rb:143); the adapter member is the include seam.
Reads the already-parsed frozen `_sessionVariables` rather than re-fetching `@config[:variables]`, which the config parse resolved once at construction.
Runs as the first step of `_performQuery`, itself the block already executing inside withRawConnection, so the SET goes to the acquired client directly rather than re-entering rawExecute's leaf loop.

The `rows.first` read is made in postgresql/database-statements.ts:333, the file matching Rails' PostgreSQL::DatabaseStatements module (postgresql/database_statements.rb:208); the adapter member is the include seam.
